Disciples already there when Paul is converted (Acts 9).
Where the disciples were first called Christians (Acts 11:26).
Paul and Barnabas preach at Salamis and Paphos (Acts 13).
Churches at Iconium, Lystra and Derbe (Acts 14).
Claudius expels Jews from Rome over “Chrestus” (Suetonius); Paul writes to the Roman church c. 57.
Lydia baptised: the first church in Europe that Acts describes (Acts 16).
Paul’s earliest surviving letter, 1 Thessalonians, c. 50.
Paul’s base for two to three years (Acts 19).
By tradition the apostle Thomas lands at Kodungallur in 52; Christians are attested in India by the 6th century.
Paul finds believers there on his way to Rome (Acts 28:14).
A church by about 100; tradition names Mark as its founder.
Ignatius writes to its church; Polycarp is its bishop.
The martyrs of Lyon and Vienne; Irenaeus becomes bishop.
The Scillitan martyrs (180), the first dated Latin Christian text.
A church building is mentioned in the flood of 201; the first Syriac-speaking Christian centre.
The oldest known house-church, with wall paintings.
Alban, the first British martyr, at Verulamium (3rd century); British bishops at Arles in 314.
King Tiridates III baptised by Gregory the Illuminator (traditional date 301).
The Council of Elvira, the earliest surviving canons of a Western council.
King Mirian III converted through Nino (c. 337).
King Ezana converts; Frumentius is consecrated bishop by Athanasius.
Ulfilas is made bishop for the Goths and translates the Bible into Gothic.
The Synod of Seleucia-Ctesiphon organises the Church of the East.
A Christian city in Arabia; its martyrs of 523 are remembered across the East.
Missions to the Nubian kingdoms begin (from 543).
Augustine reaches Canterbury; King Æthelberht is baptised.
Alopen of the Church of the East reaches the Tang capital Chang’an.
Cyril and Methodius begin the Slavonic liturgy.
Olaf II dies at Stiklestad and is venerated as the patron of Norway.
The old temple at Uppsala gives way to the church (c. 1100).
The last pagan state in Europe is baptised.
King Nzinga a Nkuwu is baptised; his son Afonso I makes Kongo a Catholic kingdom.
The first Spanish missionaries in the Americas.
Lima is founded; a diocese from 1541.
The first Jesuits arrive at Salvador.
The Spanish mission begins at Cebu.
Matteo Ricci is allowed to live in the capital.
Jamestown, with Anglican worship from the start.
Georg Schmidt’s Moravian mission at Genadendal.
Yi Seung-hun returns from Beijing baptised and founds a lay church.
The first fleet brings an Anglican chaplain to Sydney.
Black Loyalist settlers from Nova Scotia found Freetown with their own churches.
Samuel Marsden preaches at the Bay of Islands.
Samuel Ajayi Crowther’s mission at Abeokuta; he becomes bishop in 1864.
Anglican, then Catholic missionaries reach Buganda; martyrs in 1885–87.
The Azusa Street revival begins modern Pentecostalism.
By the 1970s Christianity is growing faster in sub-Saharan Africa than anywhere else; today more Christians live there than in any other continent.
